claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation temperatures of at least about 2300 °C for full densification.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 is prone to porosity and failure during service in liquid plating baths.
A liquid-precursor route can produce ultrafine ZrB2 powder.
Combining liquid-precursor-derived powder with short-dwell spark plasma sintering can consolidate single-phase ZrB2 below 2000 °C.
Controlled pyrolysis of dissolved Zr and B precursor sources forms fine, reactive ZrB2 powder.
SPS at 1800–1900 °C under uniaxial pressure and an inert atmosphere rapidly densifies the precursor-derived ZrB2 powder.
The liquid-precursor route forms nanoscale ZrB2 particles.
Nanoscale ZrB2 particles enable dense, low-porosity consolidation.
Smaller particles and grains increase reactivity and thereby reduce the sintering temperature required for ZrB2.
The precursor-plus-SPS route mitigates flaw formation in ZrB2.
A denser ZrB2 microstructure improves corrosion resistance in liquid plating media.
The proposed route will produce dense, single-phase ZrB2 below 1900 °C.
The resulting ZrB2 will have mechanical performance comparable to or better than ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C.
The resulting ZrB2 will exhibit fewer pores and fewer hole-induced failures during plating-bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Conventionally sintered ZrB2 prepared at about 2300 °C has higher porosity, weaker mechanical integrity, and greater vulnerability to prolonged fluid infiltration than the proposed material.
The applicability of liquid-precursor processing can depend on precursor or compositional compatibility.
Scale-up, fabrication of larger parts, and the cost or availability of precursor and SPS equipment may constrain the method.
